title: Warm Winey Chinese Pork Bao
description: A winey, molten Chinese dish featuring juniper berries, perfect for a hangover cure, this sugar-free-friendly recipe is a delicious and savory treat. The combination of pork, wine, and spices creates a rich and satisfying flavor profile.
instructions: In a large pan, heat the sesame oil over medium heat and cook the pork until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the crushed juniper berries, grated ginger, and cook for an additional 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the red wine, soy sauce, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture cook, covered, for 20 minutes, or until the pork is tender and the sauce has thickened.
While the pork is cooking, steam the bao buns according to the package instructions.
To assemble the baos, slice the steamed buns in half and fill with the pork mixture, topping with chopped green onions.
Serve the baos immediately, garnished with additional green onions if desired.
Let the baos cool for a few minutes before serving, allowing the filling to set.
Reheat any leftover baos in the steamer for a few minutes before serving.
